one_month_reasoning: The main event in the window is Q3 2026 results, still unconfirmed and estimated for Nov 3 pre-market (MarketBeat; Q3 2025 was Nov 4), so the reaction most likely lands before the Nov 4 scoring date. Guidance is GB $58.25-60.25B and non-GAAP EPS $0.84-0.88 against about $0.87 consensus. Base rate: Uber's average absolute earnings-day move is about 5.8%, and 6 of the last 8 were negative. The September open-market buys by the CEO ($10.0M at $70.96, Form 4) and COO ($5.3M) are verified, but insider buying is a weak 1-month signal and does not set the sign of an earnings reaction. The Delivery Hero acceptance period ends Nov 5, just outside the window. I keep a near-symmetric lognormal, median $69.9 and sigma 11% (35%/3.5 = 10%, plus a little for earnings). The ladder is unchanged from round 1.

fair_value.method: Blend of three methods on Oct-2027 NTM numbers: P/E ($4.78 haircut NTM EPS x 17.5x = $84), EV/EBITDA ($14.2B haircut NTM adj. EBITDA x 10x, net debt about 0, 2.0B shares = $71), and FCF yield ($12.5B / 7.5% = $83). Weights 0.4/0.3/0.3 give $79.6. Round 2 rebases the peer multiples to a consistent NTM basis (median ~19.6x P/E, ~9.4x EV/EBITDA).

methods.name: EV/EBITDA
methods.inputs: NTM adj. EBITDA at Oct-2027 = 0.25x$13.8B + 0.75x$16.5B = $15.8B, haircut 10% = $14.2B; x10x = $142B EV; net debt about 0 excluding Delivery Hero; 2.0B shares = $71

inputs_detail.derivation: MarketScreener EBITDA estimates (the supervisor's NTM rebuild uses the same blended $15.8B); 2026E $11.4B is consistent with Q2 $2.82B and the Q3 guide of $2.86-2.96B

The consistent NTM peer median is ~9.4x (core 7 ~8.5x; range 6.3x TCOM to 19.0x MELI). My round-1 14.7x median was mixed trailing/stale. UBER trades at 11.1x NTM. I use 10x, inside the range, between the median and BKNG at 10.2x. The small premium to the median is backed by structurally faster EBITDA growth (consensus 2027E +21%, 2028E +20%, vs BKNG/EXPE/TCOM in the low teens), which should last through the horizon. It is smaller than DASH's 17.5x premium for similar growth, and I give no credit for re-rating toward Uber's own current 11.1x. Adj. EBITDA excludes stock comp, which argues against going higher. [Citation gate 2026-10-07] [Citation gate 2026-10-07] Peer medians cited here are superseded by filings-based values: P/E 16.6x (core-7 13.3x), EV/EBITDA 9.2x (core-7 7.9x, range 4.8x TCOM to 18.6x MELI); UBER 16.7x P/E and 11.3x EV/EBITDA at the $69.48 Oct-5 close. The multiple chosen here is the agent's judgment and is unchanged. BKNG is 10.5x on the filings basis (not 10.2x). Consensus EBITDA growth +21.6% 2027E / +19.1% 2028E confirmed (src 5).

Net debt today is $4.7B (debt $12.7B, cash $5.4B plus investments). About $10B+ of annual FCF less buybacks (H1 2026 $3.5B) brings net debt to about zero. Diluted shares are 2.05B, trending lower on buybacks. Delivery Hero (closes H2 2027) is treated as value-neutral: debt-funded, with acquired EBITDA offsetting it [Citation gate 2026-10-07] $4.7B is total debt including leases ($14.73B: $12.72B debt + $2.01B operating leases) less $5.39B cash and ST investments less $4.60B marketable securities (Q2 8-K and 10-Q), not debt $12.7B less cash and investments. H1 2026 buybacks of ~$3.5B are confirmed by the CFO on the Q2 call (Q1 $3.0B + Q2 $0.51B), not by src 1 or 4.

methods.inputs: NTM FCF at Oct-2027 about $12.5B / 7.5% yield = $167B / 2.0B shares

The $12.5B estimate is unchanged.
Uber's current yield is about 7.1% (TTM FCF/market cap) and TIKR cites 8.4%. I assume no re-rating, so the market's AV discount persists

bear.story: A 2027 slowdown or recession (Kalshi 2027 recession contract ~20-23% in late Sep/early Oct 2026, down from ~39% in August) cuts trips and delivery orders, and/or Delivery Hero leverage and the >$10B AV program weigh on FCF. Consensus EPS is cut 10-15% and the multiple compresses toward ~11-12x NTM, where Lyft trades on EV/EBITDA. Waymo/Tesla direct-app growth keeps the AV overhang live, though Waymo's Austin/Atlanta app only starts Jan 2028, after the horizon.

base.story: Gross bookings grow high-teens, 2027 EPS lands near $4.4-4.5, and buybacks continue. Uber is roughly fairly valued against NTM peers, so returns come from EPS compounding, not re-rating. The AV overhang holds the multiple near 15-16x NTM. Insider buying near $71 and the usual partial mean reversion after a 30% drawdown support a modest move above spot.

bull.story: AV partners ramp on the platform, Delivery Hero closes on plan in 2H27, 2027 EPS beats and estimates rise, and the multiple moves to ~19x NTM EPS of ~$5.3 (the all-peer median), back toward the $101 52-week high.

I assume no re-rating toward the current 11.1x. thesis_break_reason: $54 is ~22% below spot, ~17% below the $65.41 52-week low, ~11x haircut NTM EPS and ~7.5x NTM EV/EBITDA (Lyft-like). Trading there would most likely mean estimates are being cut: bookings growth sliding toward ~10%, a 2027 recession hitting trips, AV players visibly taking US share before their 2028 dates, or Delivery Hero/AV spending pushing leverage well above 2x. It would also put the stock ~24% below where the CEO bought $10M in September, which argues against reading it as noise.

reasoning: Round 2. Base rates are unchanged: 35% realized vol, a -29.5% year, the stock near its $65.41 low, with history showing both deep drawdowns and strong mean reversion. The supervisor's fact-checks confirmed the operating inputs (Q2 GB +22% cc, EPS $0.81, adj. EBITDA $2.8B, TTM FCF >$10B, 2.05B shares), plus the $10.0M CEO and $5.3M COO open-market buys, which I had missed and treat as a mild positive base-rate signal. They also corrected my comps. On a consistent NTM basis peers are ~19.6x P/E and ~9.4x EV/EBITDA, not my mixed/stale 20.3x/14.7x, and Lyft's '8x' was an adjusted-EPS artefact. That raised my P/E multiple (17x to 17.5x, no longer anchored on Lyft) and cut my EBITDA multiple (11x to 10x), so the fair value moves from $80.5 to $79.6. My own checks: the Phoenix pilot did end (TechCrunch: ended May 2026, ~a dozen cars; it was a pilot ending, not an 'exclusivity' end). The Kalshi 2027 recession contract fell from ~39% (Aug 4) to an all-time low ~20% (Sep 26) and ~23% (Oct 5, search summary; market page blocked 429). I was therefore over-weighting the stress state, and, as the supervisor noted, it partly double-counted the AV bear case. Distribution: 85% lognormal median $76.5, sigma 0.30, plus 15% stress lognormal median $53, sigma 0.32 (round 1: 80/20, $77/$52). Mixture median ~$73, P(>=$70) 0.553, P(>=$104) 0.133, P(<$49) ~12%. I did not cut the upper tail the way the supervisor did. My main-state median is already below the blended fair value, and my bull case needs EPS beats, not EBITDA re-rating. I kept tail floors (P>=$17.41 = 0.997) for catastrophic outcomes. No options data was used. Research was limited to 8 extra queries; the Kalshi market page was blocked.
